PENDING ON THE FILE OF THE V ADDITIONAL DISTRICT AND SESSIONS JUDGE, D.K., MANGALORE SITTING AT PUTTUR REGISTERED FOR THE OFFENCE P/U/S 376(2)(n), 506 OF IPC AND SEC.5,6 OF POCSO ACT AND SEC. 3(1)(w)(i)(ii), 3(2)(v),

THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
ORDER WAS MADE THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MRS JUSTICE M G UMA  ORAL ORDER Petitioner being accused No.2 in Cr. No.80/2021 of Puttur Rural Police Station, now pending in Spl.
Case No.5037/2021 on the file of the learned V Addl. District and Sessions Judge, D.K., Mangaluru,
registered for the offences punishable under Sections 376(2)(n) and 506 of Indian Penal Code,
Sections 5 and 6 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, and also under Sections 3(1)(w)(i)(ii), 3(2)(V) and 3(2)(Va) of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, is seeking to quash the criminal proceedings initiated against him.
NC: 2024:KHC:45680 2.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Brief facts of the case are that, the victim aged 17 years lodged the first information with Puttur Police on 05.09.2021 against one pramod alleging that he has committed the offences from 01.02.2020 till 20.02.2021.
It is stated that the said pramod abducted her and committed sexual assault and criminally intimidated her not to reveal the said fact to anybody else.
As a result she gave birth to a child.
On the basis of same, Crime No.80/2021 was registered for the above said offences.
The victim was subjected to medical examination.
As per medical records maintained with Government Lady Goshan Hospital, Mangalore, the victim gave history alleging commission of offence by Pramod.

It appears that there was counselling made to the victim and when the statement of the victim was again recorded on 07.09.2021, she made allegations against Satish who is arrayed as accused No.1 that it was not Pramod, but it was Satish who committed the offences and responsible to impregnate her.

Subsequently, the second further statement of the victim was recorded by the Investigating NC: 2024:KHC:45680 officer, where the victim referred to the name of the petitioner as he committed the offences against her and she was impregnated, as a result of the act committed by the petitioner and later gave birth to a child.
After investigation, the charge sheet came to be filed against accused Nos.1 and 2, while dropping Pramod as referred to by the victim at the first instance.

The learned Magistrate registered S.C.No.5037/2021 and the same is Narayana Rai vs State Of Karnataka on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129774061/
2 pending for trial.

sentences.text: The petitioner being accused No.2 is before this Court seeking to quash the criminal proceedings initiated against him.
3. Heard Sri Rajashekar.S, learned counsel for the petitioner and Smt. Rashmi Jadhav, learned Addl. SPP for respondent No.1.
Perused the materials on record.

4. Learned counsel for the petitioner contended that initially, the victim lodged the first information in Crime No.80/2021 on 05.09.2021 against one Pramod alleging commission of the offences from 01.02.2020 till 20.02.2021.

When she was subjected to medical NC: 2024:KHC:45680 examination,
the victim has referred to the name of the said Pramod as responsible to impregnate her.

Thereafter,
the further statement of the victim was recorded on 07.09.2021, wherein she refers the name of satish accused No.1 and makes similar allegations stating that it was satish accused No.1 who committed the offences as stated above against her.
5. Learned counsel submits that accused No.1 has confessed regarding the commission of offences and his confessional statement was recorded by the Investigating Officer.
He submits that either in the first information or in the first further statement of the victim, there was no reference to the petitioner herein.

However, subsequently the second further statement of the victim was recorded on 24.09.2021 and for the first time, the name of the petitioner is mentioned by the victim stating that accused No.2 is also responsible for her pregnancy and stated that he has committed the offences as stated above.

Learned counsel submitted that except the second further statement of the victim regarding commission of the offences by the petitioner, there is absolutely no other material to substantiate the said contentions.

Learned counsel has drawn the attention of the Court to the First Information Report in Crime No.16/2018 of Puttur Rural Police Station, which was registered on the basis of first information lodged by the same victim on 22.02.2018 alleging commission of similar offences against one Peeresh from 01.08.2017 to 22.02.2018.
It is stated that she became pregnant as a result of the offences committed by said Peeresh.

7. Learned counsel also produced the evidence of the victim, who is examined in Spl. Case No.153/2018 registered against the said Peeresh, wherein the victim has disowned the statement made against Peeresh.
In view of all these developments, learned counsel submitted that the petitioner is aged 73 years and baseless allegations are made against him.

The conduct of the NC:
2024:KHC:45680 victim assumes importance in appreciating the veracity of her statements.
Therefore, it is a clear case of abuse of process of the Court.
Hence, he prays to allow the petition by quashing the criminal proceedings initiated against the petitioner.
8. Per contra, learned Addl. SPP submits that very serious allegations are made against the petitioner for having committed the offences.
Of course, the victim has alleged commission of the offence against three accused persons.
She submitted that as per the DNA examination, Peeresh is the biological father of the foetus and the said case is pending consideration.

However, in the Narayana Rai vs State Of Karnataka on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129774061/
3 present petition, the victim has not assisted the Investigating Officer in drawing the blood sample for DNA examination.

sentences.text: But, in view of the serious allegations made against the petitioner, the petitioner is not entitled for any relief in this petition.
Accordingly, prays for dismissal of the petition.

My answer to the above point is in the affirmative for the following;
REASONS
The victim is aged about 17 years.
She has filed first information on 05.09.2021 making specific and detailed allegations against the accused one Pramod.
The FIR in Crime No.80/2021 was registered based on the first information.

Subsequently, the further statement of the victim was recorded on 07.09.2021, wherein the victim has changed her version and made allegations against Satish who is arrayed as accused No.1, stating that it was NC: 2024:KHC:45680 he who committed the offence and was responsible to impregnate her.
The investigation was undertaken.
Accused No.1 was apprehended and his confessional statement was recorded.
As a result of which, the case against Pramod, which was initially registered came to be dropped.

However, later the second further statement of the victim was recorded on 24.09.2021 in which, for the first time the victim referred to the name of the petitioner herein and made similar allegations that he has committed forcible sexual assault on her.
However, she also refers to accused No.1 as he had also committed the offences as alleged.
Admittedly, the victim has not stated anything before the Medical Officer regarding the offences committed by the petitioner herein.

Except the second further statement of the victim,
there is absolutely nothing to support her contention regarding the commission of the offence by the petitioner.
11. Learned Addl.

SPP fairly concedes that as per the charge sheet there is absolutely no supporting - 10 - NC: 2024:KHC:45680 document or other materials to support the contention of the prosecution against the petitioner.
The victim has not co-operated in drawing the blood sample to find out the biological father of the foetus.

12. While analyzing the conduct of the victim, it is pertinent to refer to Crime No.16/2018 of Puttur Rural Police Station registered on the basis of the similar allegations against one Peeresh on 22.02.2018 alleging commission of offence from 01.08.2017 to 22.2.2018.
It is stated that DNA examination of the foetus was conducted and as per the DNA report, it is stated that said Peeresh is the biological father.

Inspite of that, the victim appears to have turned hostile while deposing before Narayana Rai vs State Of Karnataka on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129774061/
4

sentences.text: the trial court in Spl.Case No.153/2018 and stated that she has never given any statement against the said Peeresh before the learned Magistrate while giving her statement under Section 164 of Cr.P.C.
She pleaded her ignorance against the complaint given by her.
All these facts are having very serious impact on the conduct of the victim-respondent - 11 - NC: 2024:KHC:45680 No.1.

Since there are absolutely no basis for making allegations against the petitioner and there is no iota of evidence to support the contention of the victim to state that the petitioner had committed the offences as above, I am of the opinion that filing of the charge sheet against the petitioner is without any basis and it is a clear case of abuse of the process of law.

Taking in to consideration all these facts and circumstances, prima-facie I am of the opinion that victim is misusing the provisions of the Scheduled Castes and Schedules Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act,
which is a beneficial legislation.

is hereby quashed.
